title: Add CI workflow to run tests on PRs and pushes
description:
## Context

From the [PR #6 review](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-api-pkg/pull/6#pullrequestreview-2889752536), @juliasilge suggested adding CI to run the test suite:

> Would it make sense to add some CI to run the tests? Not in this PR but sometime soon?

Currently the repo only has a `release.yml` workflow for publishing. There is no CI that runs tests on PRs or pushes.

## Proposed

Add a GitHub Actions workflow (e.g. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) that:

- **Triggers** on pushes to `main` and pull requests targeting `main`
- **Runs the test suite** (`npm test`) which includes:
  - Unit tests (runtime functions, type definitions, strip-proposed-types)
  - Integration tests (`npm pack` + `tsc --noEmit` under multiple tsconfig configurations)
- **Tests across Node versions** (e.g. 18, 20, 22)
- **Requires the Positron source repo** -- the build step copies type definitions from `../positron/src/positron-dts/`, so the workflow will need to check out the Positron repo as a sibling directory

## Notes

The sibling-repo dependency is the main complexity here. Options include:
1. Checking out `posit-dev/positron` in the workflow (large repo, may need sparse checkout)
2. Caching or vendoring just the needed `.d.ts` files
3. Using the already-committed `dist/` files for test-only runs (skipping the gather step)

title: TypeScript compilation errors: missing reference path files in published package
description:
## Problem

When using `@posit-dev/positron@0.2.2` as a dev dependency, TypeScript compilation fails with errors originating from `dist/positron.d.ts`.

`positron.d.ts` contains these reference path directives:

```typescript
/// <reference path="../vscode-dts/vscode.proposed.chatProvider.d.ts" />
/// <reference path="../vscode-dts/vscode.proposed.languageModelThinkingPart.d.ts" />
```

These paths resolve relative to `dist/`, expecting files at `vscode-dts/` in the package root, but those files are not included in the published npm package.

**Errors:**
```
node_modules/@posit-dev/positron/dist/positron.d.ts(6,22): error TS6053: File '…/vscode-dts/vscode.proposed.chatProvider.d.ts' not found.
node_modules/@posit-dev/positron/dist/positron.d.ts(7,22): error TS6053: File '…/vscode-dts/vscode.proposed.languageModelThinkingPart.d.ts' not found.
```

Because those proposed API files are missing, types they declare are also unresolved, causing downstream errors:

```
node_modules/@posit-dev/positron/dist/positron.d.ts(2156,187): error TS2724: '"vscode"' has no exported member named 'LanguageModelResponsePart2'. Did you mean 'LanguageModelResponsePart'?
node_modules/@posit-dev/positron/dist/positron.d.ts(2160,88): error TS2724: '"vscode"' has no exported member named 'LanguageModelChatMessage2'. Did you mean 'LanguageModelChatMessage'?
```

These types (`LanguageModelResponsePart2`, `LanguageModelChatMessage2`) are Positron-specific proposed VS Code API types that would be defined in the missing `vscode.proposed.chatProvider.d.ts` file. They don't exist in any published version of `@types/vscode` (verified up to 1.109.0).

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev @posit-dev/positron @types/vscode typescript
```

`tsconfig.json`:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "target": "ES2023",
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

`index.ts`:
```typescript
import { tryAcquirePositronApi } from "@posit-dev/positron";
const api = tryAcquirePositronApi();
console.log(api?.version);
```

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
# 4 errors from node_modules/@posit-dev/positron/dist/positron.d.ts
```

## Expected behavior

The package should compile without errors when used as a dependency in a standard VS Code extension project. Either:

1. Include the referenced `vscode-dts/` files in the published package, or
2. Remove/inline the reference path directives so they aren't needed at compile time

## Workaround

Setting `"skipLibCheck": true` in `tsconfig.json` suppresses the errors, but this disables type checking across all declaration files which is undesirable.

## Environment

- `@posit-dev/positron`: 0.2.2
- `@types/vscode`: ^1.87.0 (also verified with 1.109.0)
- TypeScript: ^5.9.3

title: Different license needed
description: Right now this package is using the same elastic licence as positron. This makes it unable to be used in open source projects like quarto. We will need to figure out what type of license is appropriate.
